mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, investors anticipate tighter credit conditions, which reduces the present value of future earnings and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar rising-rate regimes are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10), or FEDFUNDS increase is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the CPIAUCSL inflation index by at least 0.5% over two months signals disinflation, prompting central banks to hold rates steady and boosting investor confidence in long-term growth, which elevates S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.5% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than average during neutral inflation periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a tight labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by ≥0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: Across 100 such labor market events, 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) unexpectedly jumps by at least 5% in a month, it indicates stronger consumer demand, which elevates earnings growth forecasts and supports higher S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥5% in the next month (unexpected)
failure_condition: In 10 similar positive demand shocks, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 2% signals weakening supply-side activity, which raises the risk of output shortfalls and elevates equity risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥2% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 12 such episodes, 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period when FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for three consecutive months, the persistence of high policy rates is associated with reduced risk appetite and lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In analogous regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during normal policy rates (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE below 4% combined with a sustained increase in PAYEMS of at least 8% over two months signals a strong labor market, which supports wage growth and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases by ≥8% over two months
failure_condition: Across 20 such labor market events, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than neutral (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the RSAFS (money supply growth) accelerates by more than 2% in a month, it often precedes a liquidity squeeze that raises borrowing costs and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >2% in the next month
failure_condition: In 15 similar acceleration events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during stable growth (p > 0.10).
